transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herst.
Two days out from the midterm elections, President Trump is on the move.
He'll hold rallies in two different states today before returning to the White House.
NPR's Ava Berger has more.
Just days ago, it was unclear whether Trump would be in Iowa and Kansas before the midterms.
Today, he will make stops in both locations, holding a rally first in Iowa, then Kansas.
He told reporters at a Mar-a-Lago Halloween party Saturday night how he was feeling.
I leave early tomorrow for Iowa. I leave early tomorrow for Kansas.
And then on Monday, we're doing a lot of different events to see if we can get it over.
And I feel very good. I feel like we're doing well. The country has never done better.
Trump will finish the day back at the White House. Ava Berger, NPR News, Washington.
The G20 gathering has ended in Atlanta without a joint communique
and no real consensus over what to do about food and energy security,
which has been hurt by the wars in Ukraine and Iran.
And here's Michelle Kellerman has more.
Secretary Rubio says the U.S. wants the G20 to focus on global economic stability,
but Russia's war against Ukraine and the U.S. war against Iran
are still roiling food and energy markets.
And Rubio is not ruling out a new round of strikes in Iran.
And the president's preference in any challenge around the world
is to try to solve it diplomatically and peacefully, if possible.
He recognizes there are some issues in the world that cannot be solved peacefully, unfortunately, sadly.
He says he met on the sidelines with Russia's foreign minister to talk about Ukraine.
It's not clear if Russian president Vladimir Putin will attend the G20 summit in Florida next month,
but Trump could meet with him at an international gathering in China before then.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, Atlanta.
Residents from a ravaged Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine
have been relocated to Ukrainian territory,
this after a ceasefire that was negotiated by Pope Leo and Melania Trump.
And here's Joanna Kekisses has more from southern Ukraine.
More than a dozen buses carrying hundreds of residents
evacuated from the Russian-occupied town of Alashki
crossed from Belarus into northern Ukraine,
where their families abated.
Ukrainian media broadcast emotional reunions of relatives
embracing evacuees wrapped in the blue and yellow flags of their homeland.
The residents had faced months of starvation in Alashki
after Russian troops mined the land around the town, blocking food supplies.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to a local ceasefire for the evacuations.
Some residents did choose to stay behind in Alashki
after the short truce helped get food and medical supplies into town.
Joanna Kekisses, NPR News, Mikhailayev, Ukraine.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
In Birmingham, Alabama, at least one person is dead.
Several others are injured after a shooting outside a stadium last night
after a college football game between Alabama and Em University and Alabama State,
the state's two biggest historically black universities in an annual rivalry.
Police Chief Michael Pickett.
I'm very grateful that with all the spectators and families
and things of that nature, this did occur after the game.
For the most part, it was off of the property.
Police say one person has been detained and several firearms were recovered from the scene.
Most spectators had already left the area before the shooting started.
Electric ferries are gaining attention as U.S. operators
look to reduce emissions from water transportation.
At Lake Tahoe, one company is testing a design that lifts the boats above the water.
Maria Palma of member station KUNR has more.
Ferry operators across the U.S. are exploring battery-powered vessels.
At Lake Tahoe, which straddles the border between California and Nevada,
Flight Tahoe is testing an electric hydrofoil.
It's designed by New Zealand-based company Vesev,
marking the company's first entry into the U.S.
The 10-passenger vessel uses underwater wings
to lift this hole above the water as it gains speed.
Flight Tahoe hopes to continue testing next year,
but regular service will require permits, charging infrastructure,
and connections to public transit.
For NPR News, I'm Maria Palma in Tahoe City.
[♪♪♪]

topics.text: President Trump holds rallies in Iowa and Kansas two days before the midterm elections
G20 gathering in Atlanta ends without joint communique amid food and energy security disputes
Secretary Rubio says U.S. won't rule out new strikes on Iran
Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Alashki town into Ukrainian territory under local ceasefire
Shooting outside Birmingham, Alabama stadium after Alabama State and Alabama A&M football game leaves one dead
Flight Tahoe tests electric hydrofoil ferry on Lake Tahoe as U.S. operators explore battery-powered vessels
